question: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who is indifferent to pleasure or pain
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Stoic"** means a person who can endure pain or hardship without showing their feelings or complaining. (संतोषी)

 
 
• **Example: **Despite the harsh conditions, the soldiers remained stoic and carried on with their duties.
 
 
 
• **"Indifferent to pleasure or pain"** refers to someone who does not show any emotional response to either happiness or suffering, much like a stoic person. (सुख-दुख से उदासीन)
 
 
• **Example: **She remained indifferent to pleasure or pain, never letting her emotions show.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Cynic **(निंदक): A person who believes that people are motivated purely by self-interest rather than acting for honorable or unselfish reasons.

 
 
• **Example:** The cynic in him could not believe that anyone would donate to charity without expecting something in return.
 
 
 
• **Chivalrous **(वीरता): Courteous and gallant, especially towards women.
 
 
• **Example: **He was known for his chivalrous behavior, always holding doors open for others.
 
 
 
• **Omniscient** (सर्वज्ञ): Knowing everything.
 
 
• **Example:** The novel is narrated by an omniscient narrator who knows the thoughts and feelings of all the characters.
